gap: No result ChatGPT got states how long the ANTHBOT N8 takes to bag its own rated 0.37-acre lawn once. From PCWorld's measured 742 sq ft/h that is about 22 h of mowing. It also takes 7.5 charges on Anthbot's 2,150 sq ft per charge claim, or 13.5 on PCWorld's measured roughly 1,200 sq ft per charge. That works out to about 1.35 h of bagging per 1,000 sq ft.
standout_why: Pages compared: PCWorld N8 review (cited), T3 N8 review (cited), Notebookcheck N8 review, Notebookcheck YUKA review (cited), T3 YUKA 1500 review, neointell capabilities page, mowerbotlab guide and anthbot.com N8 page (cited). PCWorld has the inputs: 1,200 sq ft in 97 min, 960 sq ft on 80% of the battery, 2,150 sq ft per charge claimed and an 80-minute charge. It never turns them into hours or charges per full cut, or into hours per 1,000 sq ft. Notebookcheck gives about 200 m² per charge but no figure for the rated area. T3 gives only the 1,500 m² recommendation. neointell and mowerbotlab give no figures for any bagging robot. ChatGPT's answer repeats '0.37 acre' as if one session covers it.
decides: This confirms the N8 as the pick and changes the advice that goes with it. While bagging, the N8 covers about 742 sq ft/h, so a 5,000 sq ft lawn takes about 6.7 h and 2–4 charges per cut, while the full 0.37 acre takes 22 h or more. The page should tell shoppers to size it to about half the rated area if they want a cut every day or two. The YUKA alternative has no sourced bagging rate or US price today, so the comparison can't flip the pick. Its 18% slope limit with the sweeper (45% without) is the deciding limit for sloped yards.

findings.note: 16,146 ÷ 2,150 = 7.5 (claim). 16,146 ÷ 1,200 = 13.5 (PCWorld measured). Notebookcheck's about 200 m² per charge gives 1,500 ÷ 200 = 7.5.

findings.note: 21.8 h mowing + (7.5 − 1) recharges × 80 min (PCWorld charge time) = 21.8 + 8.7 = 30.5 h.
